note: Published on-demand rate cards, plus live prices from Bittensor subnet 51 (Lium). Until 2026-10-29 this basket said no GPU cloud published a clean unauthenticated price JSON; that is no longer true — https://lium.io/api/executors serves every executor with its price, tier and accelerator model, no key. Those rows are now fetched over HTTP; the rate-card rows stay curated, each carrying the URL a human can check, because they are the comparison set a reader expects to see. On-demand only: spot and marketplace bids are a different product with a different risk, and mixing them would make the aggregate a blend of two markets — Lium labels these `tier`, and 36 of 130 executors were spot and excluded. Datacenter accelerators only, which is the same rule `rule.note` has always stated: including Lium's consumer RTX cards would take the basket to 94 rows with a 44x spread and a 49.5x gap, and a basket whose rows span 44x has no single price. That number is disclosed here rather than buried, because excluding rows is exactly the move a reader should be able to check.

rule.min_priced_note: How many rows must actually carry a price. A ratchet, like the anchor's own `ceiling`: the basket has thinned before, ACR-INF going from 6 to 5 priced of 10 requested with no signal anywhere, and `par.Basket.usable` sends a stranger's bill to the FLEET scale once a basket stops being usable — a scale anchors/GAP.md puts 10x to 1250x off market. Lower it deliberately in a commit, or fix the fetch. Raised 4 → 10 on 2026-10-29, in the same change as the fetch that first priced the six Lium accelerator classes: a floor left at 4 would have let the Bittensor rows vanish silently and re-medianed the four rate cards as if nothing had changed.
rule.note: Median across providers for a comparable accelerator tier.
rule.lium_thin_note: A class priced off fewer than `lium_min_executors` secure executors is marked `quality.thin` in the anchor and counted in `provenance.n_accelerator_classes_thin`; `lium_max_thin` is how many of the six classes may be thin before `--check` fails. A median over one executor is that executor's ASK, and SN51 inventory is ~93% idle, so this is a real and recurring condition rather than an outage: `NVIDIA H200 NVL` was already at n=1 in the 2026-10-29 anchor, and `NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3` went 6 to 1 inside 24h on 2026-10-30. The thin row is still PRICED on purpose -- dropping it would put the basket under `min_priced` above, which flips `par.Basket.usable` and reprices an outsider's bill onto the fleet's own quotes, 10x to 1250x off market by anchors/GAP.md. One disclosed thin row inside a ten-row median is a far smaller error than that. Ceiling set at 2 (measured 1 at the 2026-10-29 anchor, 2 live the next day); lower it deliberately in a commit.
rule.lium_note: `lium_tier` is the on-demand product; `lium_accelerators` is the substring set that defines 'comparable tier'. Both are declared here rather than hard-coded in scripts/anchors.py so a reader can see what was included without reading the fetcher.
